Ten Odia lines are published here out of seventeen drafted — every word traced to a headword in Praharaj's Purnnachandra Odia Bhashakosha, and seven cut with the dictionary evidence given.

faqs.question: When is Propose Day in 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday 8 February 2027. It is the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February, and Valentine's Day itself falls on Sunday 14 February.

faqs.question: How do you say "I love you" in Odia?
faqs.answer: ମୁଁ ତୁମକୁ ଭଲ ପାଉଛି (Muñ tumaku bhala pāuchi). Odia builds it on ଭଲ ପାଇବା, literally "to find good", which Praharaj's dictionary glosses at page 6055 as "To love".

faqs.question: Is Odia just a version of Bengali?
faqs.answer: No. They are siblings. Manish Minz's 2015 Typography Day paper traces both modern scripts back to proto-Odia, used from the 11th to the 14th century, after which Bengali kept the horizontal head-line and Odia curved it away. Different language, different script, different literature.

faqs.question: Should I use tu or tume when I propose in Odia?
faqs.answer: Tume (ତୁମେ), unless you are already very close. Kalyanamalini Sahoo's 2013 study lists tume as the form used for colleagues, neighbours and strangers of the same age-group, while tu carries no honorific content and is also used for servants.

faqs.question: Will Odia text show up properly on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. The Odia block sits at U+0B00 to U+0B7F in Unicode, so the message travels as real text rather than as an image. The recipient's phone still needs an Odia font, which current Android and iOS ship; a very old handset may show empty boxes.

faqs.question: What does prastaba mean in Odia?
faqs.answer: Not a romantic proposal. Praharaj glosses ପ୍ରସ୍ତାବ as "Subject; matter; topic", "Chapter; section" and "Discussion", and its single occurrence in the Universal Dependencies Odia treebank is a proposal from a bank board.

faqs.question: Can I send a Propose Day message in Sambalpuri instead?
faqs.answer: Not from this page. Sambalpuri is one of eight Odia regional varieties named in a 2026 study by Panda and Jayaraj of IIT Indore, and there is no published Sambalpuri dictionary here to check lines against, so nothing Sambalpuri is offered.

faqs.question: Is Odia a classical language of India?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Central Institute of Indian Languages, under the Ministry of Education, lists Odia among the classical languages with its own Centre of Excellence, alongside Kannada, Malayalam and Telugu.

faqs.question: Is the palm-leaf explanation for the round Odia letters actually proven?
faqs.answer: Not as far as I could verify. Minz's 2015 paper reports it with the words "it is said that", and the Unicode Standard's related remark about palm leaves and letter shapes is hedged and covers South Indian scripts generally. It is the standard explanation, not a demonstrated one.

faqs.question: How many lines were cut, and why?
faqs.answer: Seven of seventeen. Examples: ସାଥେ and ପ୍ରେମିକା return no headword in Praharaj at all; ବାହା is marked rural for marriage and otherwise means "arm"; and the bare imperative ରହ shares a headword whose first gloss is "coition".

faqs.question: Should I propose in Odia or in English?
faqs.answer: In Odia only if you already know which pronoun they use with you. Sahoo's finding is that communities of practice, not individuals, decide what counts as polite in Odia, so guessing the register is riskier than writing plainly in English.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Wishes in Odia, Checked Against a Dictionary

Propose Day 2027 falls on **Monday 8 February**, and below are ten Propose Day wishes in Odia — each in ଓଡ଼ିଆ script, with a Roman transliteration and an English meaning. Every word was looked up in Praharaj's *Purnnachandra Odia Bhashakosha*, and every verb ending matched to a form occurring in the Universal Dependencies Odia treebank or in Tatoeba's Odia sentences.

Two SubhSandesh figures set expectations, both platform-wide across 21 page types rather than proposal-specific: 5,148 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12, and 48.3% of shared pages opened on a phone (27,499 of 56,886 views). A handset is where the Odia must render.

Seven further lines were drafted and cut. This page gives the ten that survived, the ତୁ / ତୁମେ / ଆପଣ register choice, why Odia letters are shaped as they are, and what could not be verified.

## What an Odia Propose Day wish is, and which "propose" it means

An Odia Propose Day wish is a short message in the Odia script for 8 February, the second day of Valentine week. It is usually sent as a WhatsApp message or an Instagram caption, and read rather than spoken.

The word matters. In Indian usage "propose" almost always means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend, not to marry you. Odia has no neat native verb for it either: Praharaj glosses ପ୍ରସ୍ତାବ (*prastāba*) as "Subject; matter; topic", "Chapter; section" and "Discussion" — no romantic sense at all, and its one occurrence in the Odia treebank is a proposal from a bank board. Line 3, which asks someone to be your ସାଙ୍ଗ, is what most people searching this want to say.

## Ten Propose Day wishes in Odia, with transliteration and meaning

Each entry gives the line, the gloss, who it suits and how it was checked. All ten sit at the **ତୁମ** level; the register section explains why.

### 1. ମୁଁ ତୁମକୁ ଭଲ ପାଉଛି ।

*Muñ tumaku bhala pāuchi* — "I love you." Odia uses ଭଲ ପାଇବା, literally "to find good". For someone you have already told, or are telling plainly for the first time. Praharaj lists it at p. 6055 as "To love"; the `-ଉଛି` first-person ending is in the treebank in ମୁଁ … ଯାଉଛି.

### 2. ତୁମେ ମୋ ଜୀବନ ।

*Tume mo jībana* — "You are my life." Less of an overstatement than it looks: Praharaj's ଜୀବନ entry (p. 3005) gives sense 7 as "One's dearest person; beloved person". Short enough for a status.

### 3. ତୁମେ ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗ ହେବ କି ?

*Tume mo sāṅga heba ki?* — "Will you be my companion?" The real Propose Day ask, put as a question. ସାଙ୍ଗ is at p. 8361, "Companionship; companion"; the second-person future `-ବ` is in the treebank as ତୁମେମାନେ … ବଡ଼ ହେବ, the particle କି as ଦେଖିଲ କି ?

### 4. ଆଜି ମୁଁ ତୁମକୁ ଗୋଟିଏ କଥା କହିବି ।

*Āji muñ tumaku goṭie kathā kahibi* — "Today I'll tell you one thing." An opener, sent before the real message. Praharaj marks ଗୋଟିଏ ଆଦରାର୍ଥକ, the respectful counting word, against ଗୋଟାଏ, the disrespectful one.

### 5. ମୁଁ ତୁମ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ରହିବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଛି ।

*Muñ tuma sāṅgare rahibāku cāhuñchi* — "I want to stay with you." Less dramatic than line 2 and easier to answer, which is the point. ସାଙ୍ଗରେ and ରହିବ are both in the treebank; so is the want-frame, spelled ଚାହୁଁଚି there.

### 6. ମୋ ମନ ତୁମ ପାଖରେ ।

*Mo mana tuma pākhare* — "My heart is with you." Four words, no verb, nothing to misread. Good for a caption where a longer line wraps. ମନ is at p. 6253; ପାଖ at p. 4707, "Nearness; proximity".

### 7. ତୁମ ହସ ମୋ ଦିନର ସବୁଠାରୁ ଭଲ କଥା ।

*Tuma hasa mo dinara sabuṭhāru bhala kathā* — "Your laugh is the best thing in my day." Specific rather than declarative, so it works where lines 1 and 2 would be too much too soon. ହସ is at p. 9015, "Laugh; laughter"; ସବୁଠାରୁ ଭଲ is in the treebank as ସବୁଠାରୁ ଭଲ କାମ ଥିଲା.

### 8. ମୁଁ ତୁମର ଉତ୍ତର ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରିବି ।

*Muñ tumara uttara apekṣā karibi* — "I will wait for your answer." Send it after the ask, not instead. ଉତ୍ତର is at p. 945, "Reply; answer"; ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରିବା at p. 395, "To wait; to await".

### 9. ତୁମେ ଯାହା ଉତ୍ତର ଦେବ, ମୁଁ ମାନିବି ।

*Tume yāhā uttara deba, muñ mānibi* — "Whatever answer you give, I will accept it." The line worth sending. ମାନିବା is at p. 6471, "To obey; to comply with". If the answer is no, this is the last message, not the first of several.

### 10. ମୁଁ ତୁମକୁ ବିବାହ କରିବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଛି ।

*Muñ tumaku bibāha karibāku cāhuñchi* — "I want to marry you." The marriage version, for the minority of 8 February messages that mean it. ବିବାହ is at p. 5688, "Marriage; wedding"; the treebank sentence ମୁଁ ବିବାହ କରିବି ନାହିଁ has the same frame.

If the ask deserves more than a block of text, the [Will You Marry Me? proposal scrapbook](/proposal) is built for line 10 — your story, ending in a YES button that grows every time they dodge it. For lines 1 to 9, the girlfriend-or-boyfriend ask, the ["I love you" page](/love-gf) fits better: third most-created page type at 1,178 pages, 22.9% of everything created, and most-viewed at 16,998 views, 29.9% of all page views. Both interfaces are English: they carry your Odia, they do not write or check it.

## ତୁ, ତୁମେ or ଆପଣ: the choice that decides whether a line lands

Odia has three second-person singular pronouns, and the wrong one is what a native reader notices first. Kalyanamalini Sahoo's 2013 study in *Acta Linguistica Asiatica* sets out all three with their agreement.

**ତୁ** (*tu*) is intimate — close friends, relatives, younger people. Sahoo records that, lacking honorific content, it is also used for servants and "socially low class people". None of the ten lines uses it. Praharaj is blunter, glossing ତୁ "Thou (contemptuously used)".

**ତୁମେ** (*tume*) sits between them, and Sahoo lists its users precisely: in-laws, male family members, colleagues, **strangers of the same age-group**, neighbours, elders. Someone you are about to propose to is almost by definition in that band.

**ଆପଣ** (*āpaṇa*) is the honorific, the one students use for a teacher, and takes its own ending — the imperative `-ନ୍ତୁ`, as in the treebank's ଆପଣ ଗରମ ପାଣି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ. Line 3 becomes **ଆପଣ ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗ ହେବେ କି ?** Use it if you have only ever addressed them formally.

## Why Odia letters are round, and why that matters on a phone

The curved, umbrella-hooked Odia letters are usually explained by palm leaf. Manish Minz's 2015 Typography Day paper records the mechanics: Odia was incised on dried palm leaves called *Tari* with a metal stylus, a *Kitta lekhani*, the grooves rubbed with carbon-based ink and cleaned with sand. The paper says Bengali "retained the horizontal tip line of the original script" while "it is said that Odia script changed them to curves due to the exigencies of the writing material, the palm leaf".

Note the hedge. Minz reports that explanation rather than demonstrating it, and the Unicode Standard's related remark about palm leaves and letter shapes covers South Indian scripts generally. I found nothing proving it for Odia, so I will not assert it.

What is settled: Odia and Bengali are siblings, not variants. Minz traces both to proto-Odia, used from the 11th to the 14th century across Assam, Bengal and Odisha, with Odia's script fully formed under the Suryavanshi kings of 1435–1540. Odia is also a classical language: the Central Institute of Indian Languages, under the Ministry of Education, lists it with Kannada, Malayalam and Telugu, each with a Centre of Excellence.

Practically, that means rendering. The Odia block sits at U+0B00–U+0B7F, so these lines travel as text, not pictures — but the phone needs an Odia font. Android and iOS ship one; a very old handset may show boxes.

## Which Odia are you actually writing?

There is more than one. A 2026 paper by Dibya Prakash Panda and Thapasya Jayaraj of IIT Indore, in *Annali di Ca' Foscari: Serie Orientale*, calls Odia a continuum of regional varieties and analyses negation across eight: Kataki, Sambalpuri, Debagadia, Sundargadi, Singhbhumi, Baleswari, Desia and Ganjami. It is forthcoming and only the abstract is readable, so eight is all I take from it.

These ten lines are standard Odia. Someone who reads Sambalpuri at home will understand them, but as school Odia rather than as theirs.

## Four ways to send an Odia line, compared

The container decides whether the script survives, and who can read it.

| Delivery | Odia script | Who can open it | Platform-wide figure (21 page types) |
|---|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp message | Unicode text, U+0B00–U+0B7F | Anyone in the chat | Not measurable by us |
| Instagram caption or story | Unicode text | Followers, plus reshares | Not measurable by us |
| Screenshot or image | Pixels — not copyable | Anyone, no font needed | Not measurable by us |
| A shareable SubhSandesh page | Unicode text in the page | Whoever has the link | 48.3% of 56,886 views on a phone; 38.5% password-protect before sharing (1,983 of 5,148) |

A screenshot is the only option that survives a missing font, and the only one they cannot copy, search or reply to inline.

## When an Odia line is the wrong thing to send

If you are in the same room, say it out loud. A written line is for distance, and 8 February 2027 is a working Monday — but it is not an improvement on speech.

If you do not know which pronoun they use with you, an Odia line is a guess dressed as a gesture. Sahoo's finding is that communities of practice, not individuals, decide what counts as polite. Ask a mutual friend, or write in English.

If the answer is no, line 9 is where it ends. A refusal is information, not an obstacle.

## Sources

- Kalyanamalini Sahoo, "Pronouns, Address Forms and Politeness Strategies in Odia", [*Acta Linguistica Asiatica* 3(1)](https://journals.uni-lj.si/ala/article/view/65), 28 June 2013. Open access, full text read.
- Manish Minz, ["A calligraphic approach to Odia script"](https://www.typoday.in/2015/spk_papers/Manish%20Minz-Typographyday2015.pdf), Typography Day 2015. Full paper read.
- [Classical Languages](https://www.ciil.org/clalanguages.php), Central Institute of Indian Languages, Ministry of Education, Government of India. The page gives no publication date.
- Dibya Prakash Panda and Thapasya Jayaraj, ["Negation in Regional Varieties of Odia"](https://edizionicafoscari.unive.it/en/edizioni4/riviste/annali-di-ca-foscari-serie-orientale/2026/62/negation-in-regional-varieties-of-odia-synchronic/), *Annali di Ca' Foscari: Serie Orientale* 62, 2026. Accepted 24 June 2026, forthcoming, abstract only.
- Verification instruments, credited not cited: Praharaj's *Purnnachandra Odia Bhashakosha* via [Digital Dictionaries of South Asia](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/praharaj/); the [Universal Dependencies Odia ODTB treebank](https://universaldependencies.org/treebanks/or_odtb/), 456 sentences, 5,818 tokens; Tatoeba's 402 Odia sentences; Unicode Standard chapter 12.

Full text read via the PDF galley /ala/article/download/65/324 on 2026-09-24; data from the EMILLE/CIIL corpus plus the author's native-speaker judgements.

Odia was incised on dried palm leaves called Tari with a metal stylus (Kitta lekhani / Loha kantaka), the grooves then rubbed with carbon-based ink and cleaned with sand; Bengali "retained the horizontal tip line of the original script" while "it is said that Odia script changed them to curves due to the exigencies of the writing material, the palm leaf" — the paper reports the palm-leaf explanation with that hedge rather than demonstrating it. Full PDF text extracted and read on 2026-09-24.

Page fetched 2026-09-24; it publishes no publication date (it shows "Last updated on : 20/08/2024", a modification date), so publishedDate is omitted.

Open access, peer reviewed, CC BY, Panda and Jayaraj (IIT Indore). odiaLedger.method: Every published line decomposes into (a) headwords found in Praharaj's Purnnachandra Odia Bhashakosha via the Digital Dictionaries of South Asia, queried one headword at a time, and (b) a verb ending attested in UD Odia-ODTB (456 sentences, 5,818 tokens, pulled as CoNLL-U) or in Tatoeba's 402 Odia sentences. No line was written from memory or intuition.
cuts: ତୁ ମୋ ଜୀବନ — Sahoo (2013, full text) records that tu lacks honorific content and is used for servants and "socially low class people"; Praharaj glosses ତୁ (p. 3498) "Thou (contemptuously used)". Wrong pronoun for an ask.
ମୁଁ ତୁମ ସାଥେ ରହିବି — ସାଥେ returns no headword in Praharaj, and neither does ସାଥୀ. Hindi/Bengali-shaped. Replaced throughout with ସାଙ୍ଗ / ସାଙ୍ଗରେ.
ତୁମେ ମୋ ପ୍ରେମିକା — ପ୍ରେମିକା returns no headword in Praharaj.

ମୁଁ ତୁମକୁ ବାହା ହେବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଛି — Praharaj marks ବାହା (p. 5578) ଗ୍ରା. (rural/colloquial) for marriage and its ordinary sense is "Arm; strength". Replaced with ବିବାହ (p. 5688), which the treebank also attests.
ରହ ମୋ ପାଖରେ — Praharaj's headword ରହ (p. 7029) opens on "Coition; copulation", the Odia imperative appearing only later in the entry. Same failure mode as the wave-3 Kannada ಬಾಳು cut.

ମୁଁ ତୁମକୁ ଚାହେଁ — Praharaj glosses ଚାହିଁବା (p. 2634) "to look at; to see; to wait in expectation", not "to desire". Only the ...ବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଛି frame was kept, which the treebank attests in the modern want sense.
ତୁମେ ଖୁସିରେ ରୁହ — ଖୁସି is attested (p. 2020, a Persian loan) but Praharaj also records a ଗ୍ରା. sense that is crude, and ରୁହ inherits the ରହ problem.

structuralLimitations: THE ODIA WAS NOT REVIEWED BY A NATIVE SPEAKER. Every line is verified against published instruments — Praharaj's dictionary, the UD Odia treebank, Tatoeba and Sahoo (2013) — but verification is not the same as a fluent reader's judgement of whether a line sounds natural in a proposal. Have a native speaker read it before sending it.

Odia resources are materially thinner than for Hindi, Bengali or Marathi. The entire UD Odia-ODTB treebank is 456 sentences and 5,818 tokens, its genre is nonfiction and news, and it contains ZERO instances of ତୁ and ZERO of singular ତୁମେ (one ତୁମ, one ତୁମେମାନେ, two ଆପଣ). Tatoeba holds 402 Odia sentences. Second-person agreement had to be taken from those four Tatoeba sentences plus Sahoo's worked examples, not from a large corpus.

Praharaj's Purnnachandra Odia Bhashakosha was compiled 1931-1940. Its glosses are authoritative for attestation but can lag modern usage — the clearest case here is ଚାହିଁବା, which Praharaj glosses only as "to look at / to wait" while the treebank attests a modern "want" sense (ମୁଁ ... ଚାହୁଁଚି). Where dictionary and corpus disagree, the post says so rather than choosing silently.

Spelling variant carried into the body: the treebank writes the first-person "want" ଚାହୁଁଚି; the published lines use the standard ଚାହୁଁଛି. The -ଛି ending is separately attested (ODTB ଦେଖିପାରୁଛି; Tatoeba ତୁମେ ... ଭାବୁଛ) even though that exact spelling is not.

The palm-leaf explanation for the rounded Odia letterforms is REPORTED, NOT DEMONSTRATED. Minz (2015) states it with the hedge "it is said that"; the Unicode Standard's related remark is "Some scholars suggest..." and is about South Indian scripts generally rather than Odia specifically. No source I could fetch proves it. The body says this in prose.

Odia's classical-language status IS verified (CIIL, Ministry of Education, lists it with a Centre of Excellence; Minz records it independently), but I could not fetch a primary notification carrying the designation DATE, so the post gives no date for it.

Exempt instruments used under the BRIEF's 2026-09-24 exemption and credited in prose rather than spending sources slots: Praharaj / DSAL (dsal.uchicago.edu), UD Odia-ODTB (universaldependencies.org), Tatoeba, and chapter 12 of the Unicode Standard. Deliberate reuse, noted here so it is visible.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Two prefixes of ordinal demand — this is a low-volume, copy-text query, and a page at this volume is a visibility asset judged on impressions and on being the page an answer engine quotes when someone asks how to say this in Odia, not a converting page. The searcher copies a line and leaves. Target position 6-10, not 3: the February Valentine-week SERP is an annual news cycle owned by MensXP, Zee, Webdunia and Times Now, and this domain has neither their authority nor their backlinks. What it does have that none of them do is a line-by-line audit trail — ten lines traced to Praharaj headwords and treebank-attested verb endings, seven cuts published with the evidence, and an explicit refusal to assert the palm-leaf story as proven. That is the citable asset. It cannot be checked by a native speaker here, which is the honest ceiling on it; and ranking takes months regardless.
